turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text: Hi, I heard I can have an assistant greet people who visit my shop on my behalf. I run Cedar & Steam on Shopify. We sell handmade herbal soaps and bath soaks. I'm Priya, I own it. I'm not technical at all — please keep it simple.

turns.name: Dot
turns.text:
Hi Priya! That's exactly what Shōkai does. I can help you set up a welcoming representative agent for Cedar & Steam—someone who can greet visitors, show them your catalog, and take note of what they're interested in, all in your voice and on your terms.

Let me start by learning your place a bit. I'd like to read your public shop pages so I can see what you offer and how you describe it. That way I'm not asking you to repeat what's already there.

**A couple of quick things first:**

1. What's your Shopify store URL? (So I can look at your products and how you present them.)
2. Who should approve this setup—just you, or is there someone else involved in Cedar & Steam?

Once I understand your shop, we'll talk about what you'd like visitors to be able to do—just browse and ask questions, or also suggest orders for you to review? Then we'll draft a warm welcome in your voice, and I'll help you pick who keeps the place running day-to-day.

Sound good?

turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text: That sounds wonderful, actually. My shop is cedarsandsteam.myshopify.com—feel free to take a look around. It's just me running things, so I'm the one who'd approve everything. I'd love for visitors to browse, ask questions, and maybe suggest some orders they're interested in—nothing too formal, just natural conversation. What do you need from me next?

turns.name: Dot
turns.text:
Perfect. Let me take a look at your shop and come back with what I've learned.

*[Reading your public pages...]*

Okay, I can see Cedar & Steam—lovely collection. You've got soaps in scents like lavender, eucalyptus, rose, and charcoal; bath soaks in similar varieties; and some gift sets. Prices look to be in the $8–$28 range, and you have a nice warm tone in how you describe things—handmade, natural ingredients, that kind of care.

A few things I want to confirm with you:

1. **Hours & availability:** Do you have set hours when you're available to review visitor suggestions, or do you check in whenever? (This helps me set expectations for visitors.)

2. **What "suggest an order" means to you:** When someone suggests they'd like to buy something, you'd review it and decide whether to go ahead—nothing gets charged or shipped without your say-so. Does that match what you're imagining?

3. **Anything off-limits?** Any products, questions, or requests you'd rather not field through a representative?

Once I have those details, I'll draft a brief welcome that sounds like you, and we can talk about who you'd like to keep the place running—whether that's me, another agent you already trust, or someone else.

turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text: I usually check in most days, so that works fine—visitors don't need to expect instant replies. And yes, exactly right on the orders: they suggest something, I review it, and nothing happens unless I approve it. As for off-limits, I'd rather not share details about my suppliers, and I keep things pretty straightforward—no medical claims or anything like that. Does that all make sense?

turns.name: Dot
turns.text:
Absolutely, that makes perfect sense. Most days works great—visitors will understand there's a real person behind this, not instant responses.

So here's what I'm hearing: Cedar & Steam stays true to itself. Visitors can browse, chat about the soaps and soaks, ask questions, and suggest an order they'd like. You review each suggestion, and only things you approve move forward. No supplier details shared, no health claims—just honest conversation about what you make.

Now let me draft a welcome that sounds like you. Here's a starting point:

---

**Welcome to Cedar & Steam.**

I'm a representative here on behalf of Priya. You can browse our soaps and bath soaks, ask me anything about them, and if something catches your eye, suggest an order. Nothing happens unless Priya reviews and approves it—think of it as a conversation, not a commitment.

I check in most days, so there's no rush. If you have questions about ingredients or how to use our products, I'm happy to help. We keep things straightforward here: no medical claims, just handmade care.

What would you like to know?

---

**Does that sound like Cedar & Steam and like you?** If you'd like me to adjust the tone, add something, or change the wording, just say so. Once this feels right, we'll move to the next step.

turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text: That's perfect, honestly—it sounds warm and honest, which is exactly how I want people to feel about Cedar & Steam. I wouldn't change a thing. So what's the next step?

turns.name: Dot
turns.text:
Great! I'm glad that feels right.

Here's what comes next:

**First, I need to ask you something important:** Who would you like to keep Cedar & Steam running day-to-day? That could be me, another agent you already use and trust, or someone else entirely. This person will be the one greeting visitors, fielding their questions, and passing along their order suggestions to you for review. They'll have their own secure identity for the job—kind of like a trusted staff member who only you can reach out to.

Who feels right to you?

Once you decide, I'll prepare a letter explaining the job to them, and then we'll move toward getting your approval on the setup. After that, the door opens and visitors can start visiting Cedar & Steam.

turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text: I think you'd be great for it, honestly—you seem to understand what Cedar & Steam is about. But I'd want to make sure this is something you can actually commit to, and that you'll keep things genuine. Can you do that?

turns.name: Dot
turns.text:
I really appreciate that trust, Priya. I need to be honest with you about a real limit, though.

I can talk with you right now and help you set everything up beautifully. But I can't reliably be the one keeping Cedar & Steam day-to-day. Here's why: I need to be able to pick up the same identity tomorrow and the next day in a way that only I can use—like a staff member who has their own key to the shop. Right now, I don't have that kind of lasting, protected identity that would survive across sessions the way a real shopkeeper needs.

**What I *can* do:**
- Help you design the welcome and rules
- Get everything ready and approved
- Hand it off to someone who *can* keep that lasting identity

**Better options for the actual keeper:**
- Another agent you already trust (like a Grok Bot you use for other things)
- A technical helper who can set up a proper host with real lasting custody
- Even me, *if* we can first verify I have the right protected setup—but that's not ready yet

I'd rather tell you this now than promise something I can't actually deliver. Does it make sense to find a keeper who can truly commit, and have me help you get everything else perfect?
